title: Design a read-only key-rotation and trust-impact explorer
stage: V3 design; prototype only with synthetic graph
body:
## Outcome and bounded question
Determine the smallest read-only CLI/TUI/web view that explains a proposed root/issuer/leaf rotation's affected trust paths, consumers, expiry, stale acknowledgements and rollback path without acquiring signing authority. This extends ROOT-02/04's graph model; it does not replace it or implement a portal.

## Prior art and current evidence
The spec names DOT/Mermaid/SVG/static Markdown and requires read-only-first. Candidate graph renderers are Graphviz (https://graphviz.org/documentation/) and Mermaid (https://mermaid.js.org/intro/); these links are references, not independently fetched in this task. Existing ROOT-02/04 own identity/graph records; CERT-08 owns rotation state; OPS-11 owns runbooks. No viewer exists per the package census.

## Question, API and formats
Compare a deterministic `fleet cert graph --format dot|mermaid|json` export and a read-only explorer over a versioned graph snapshot. Define nodes/edges, stable IDs, provenance, redaction, filters, impact query, snapshot freshness and pagination. No arbitrary secret metadata or private key bytes in graph payloads.

## Acceptance, tests and oracle
Use a fixed synthetic graph with cross-signs, two issuer partitions, a revoked edge, stale consumer and a proposed replacement. Require deterministic output, correct reachable-path and impact sets versus a small reference graph traversal, and explicit unknown/stale state. Negative tests: hidden signer edge, cycles, duplicate IDs, stale snapshot, malicious labels/HTML, private key fields and viewer input attempting mutation must not create authority or execute actions. Oracle is exact expected node/edge/impact set plus read-only API permission audit.

Complexity M; risks are misleading graph simplification, privacy leakage and accidental write affordance. Gate any interactive action behind separate transaction-bound OPS/CERT authorization; initial deliverable is export-only. title: Specify typed event and artifact stream connectors

## Outcome and bounded question
Define whether Fleet needs independently typed EventSink, ArtifactSink and SecretStore connector contracts for NATS JetStream, Redis, PostgreSQL/Supabase and S3-compatible object stores, and which one small synthetic adapter proves the contract. title: Separate ML-KEM hybrid transport assurance from signature policy

Determine which pinned TLS/client stacks support ML-KEM and specified hybrid key establishment, and define a transport confidentiality matrix strictly separate from certificate signature algorithms, ML-DSA-44 baseline, and optional MTC. No protocol implementation or production TLS change.

## Prior art and evidence
NIST FIPS 203 is the primary ML-KEM standard: https://csrc.nist.gov/pubs/fips/203/final. TLS hybrid groups are specified by IETF drafts/RFCs; exact current status and implementation versions must be rechecked at execution. OpenSSL provider and browser/client matrices are owned by OPS-09. ## Outcome and bounded question
Decide whether Fleet has a concrete OpenPGP certificate/subkey user outcome and, if so, identify a native typed API and independent interoperability profile without mapping OpenPGP trust onto X.509.

## Prior art
OpenPGP is standardized in RFC 9580 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc9580; GnuPG manual https://www.gnupg.org/documentation/manuals/gnupg/ is implementation reference. Links are not fetched in this task.

Map primary/subkey roles, certifications, expiry, revocation, transferable public/secret key encodings, algorithm support and trust model. Propose distinct `OpenPgpCertificate` and subkey capability types; no generic conversion from X.509 or JOSE.

## Acceptance and oracle
Round-trip synthetic key fixtures with GnuPG and one independent library, verifying signatures, subkey binding, expiry and revocation. Negative cases: wrong subkey usage, forged binding signature, expired/revoked key, unsupported algorithm and cross-format conversion request fail closed. Oracle: independent tool output plus RFC fixture expectations.

title: Specify JOSE/JWK/JWT signing and verification as a native format family
stage: V3 standards review and fixture interoperability
body:
## Outcome and bounded question
Determine whether Fleet needs native JOSE signing/key publication for a specific relying party, and define claims, audience, key ID, rotation and verification boundaries. A JWT is not a certificate and does not grant authorization by itself.

## Prior art
JWS RFC 7515 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7515, JWK RFC 7517 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7517, JWT RFC 7519 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc7519 and JWT BCP RFC 8725 https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc8725. Not fetched in this task.

## API/formats
Compare compact/JSON JWS and JWKS publication. Propose typed `JwkRef`, `JwtClaims` allowlist, `aud`, `iss`, `exp`, `nbf`, `kid` and algorithm policy. Disallow `none`, algorithm confusion, arbitrary claim injection and key-as-authorization semantics.

## Acceptance/oracle
Verify fixtures with an independent JOSE implementation; test key rotation overlap and stale JWKS cache. Negative cases: wrong audience/issuer, expired/not-yet-valid token, duplicate claims, algorithm substitution, unknown `kid`, `none`, replay and unauthorized claim must fail. Oracle: independent verifier plus exact expected policy decisions.

title: Design native OpenSSH user and host CA lifecycle
stage: V3 synthetic issuer design
body:
## Outcome and bounded question
Determine whether a separate OpenSSH CA is needed for user/host access and define principal, validity, revocation and trust distribution semantics without treating SSH certificates as X.509. GEN-05/09 own key material and rotation, not CA issuance.

## Prior art
OpenSSH certificate manual https://man.openbsd.org/ssh-keygen and sshd_config TrustedUserCAKeys/RevokedKeys https://man.openbsd.org/sshd_config. These are references, not fetched here.

Propose distinct SSH certificate profile with user/host principal allowlist, critical options/extensions, bounded validity, serial, CA fingerprint and known_hosts `@cert-authority` publication. Separate signer identity from ordinary key generation and enforce ARCH-06 transaction authority.

## Acceptance/oracle
Use synthetic keys/certs and OpenSSH `ssh-keygen`/client verifier. Prove expected user and host auth; negative cases wrong principal, host/user type confusion, expired cert, untrusted CA, revoked serial/key, forbidden forwarding option and old-key replay fail. ## Outcome / bounded question
Determine whether reusable typed config/file templates are needed beyond GEN-01/02/03's in-memory artifact, password and ID APIs, and define safe deterministic rendering without generating a second command surface.

## API / formats
Compare typed template data with deterministic JSON/YAML/TOML renderers; specify variable schema, defaults, required inputs, secret classification, output filename/mode and versioned template ID. Determinism applies to rendering for identical inputs; random secret generation remains explicit and uses vetted CSPRNG APIs.

## Minimal probe / acceptance
Render one synthetic service config twice from identical inputs and require byte-identical output; change one typed variable and require only expected semantic diff. Distinguish archive integrity from freshness and authorization.

Use synthetic low-risk values only: export from one fake store, restore to a disconnected second fake store, migrate manifest format and compare plaintext fixture hashes in protected test process. body:
## Outcome / bounded question: Design an air-gapped CSR/request package lifecycle to export a finite authorized request, transfer it with media hygiene, import the signed result and resume safely without replay. This is distinct from ROOT-10/12 escrow/ceremony and OPS-01/03 generic transactions. ## Current evidence: Spec §§11.3/15.3 require resumable offline signing, CSR bundles, air-gapped request packages, media hygiene and replay guards; no current proposal accepts this whole lifecycle. ARCH-06 finite signer tuples and exact three-destination ROOT escrow are constraints, not blockers. External protocol/media sources are unverified unless explicitly fetched later. ## API/formats: Compare a versioned manifest plus CSR/DER/PEM, detached authorization, nonce/request ID, tuple-set digest, signer receipt and return bundle. The approved signature tuple and every synthetic request fixture pin `signature_algorithm=ML-DSA-44`; no alternate PQ algorithm is in scope. Define export/inspect/verify/import/resume operations, public/private classification, media/transport custody, offline signer and online completion owner. Root private keys do not travel in request packages. ## Minimal probe/acceptance: Use a synthetic test CA and two isolated directories with removable-media simulation. Export one ML-DSA-44 tuple, verify offline, sign with a fake ARCH-06-compatible signer configured for ML-DSA-44, import and resume after crashes at export/transport/consume/sign/return/import. Oracle: canonical package digest, consumed-tuple journal and independent certificate/signature verification using a pinned verifier that explicitly supports ML-DSA-44. If no pinned independent verifier supports the baseline, report unsupported/inconclusive and stop; do not substitute a different PQ signature. Negative tamper, wrong signer/subject/validity/algorithm, any non-ML-DSA-44 substitution, duplicate import, replay, stale request, swapped media, missing receipt, unsupported verifier and uncertain signer result must block or be reported unsupported/inconclusive; never blindly reissue. ## Complexity/risks/gates/rollback: L/XL; media compromise, replay, split-brain status and lost custody. Research proceeds independently; any real ceremony requires explicit owner approval, witnessed procedure, recovery proof and ROOT-12/CERT-18 gates.
